events.text: You wake one morning and the sword is not in your hand; it is in the way you reach for a cup. An old swordsman watching you pour says, quietly, that you have begun to understand what a sword is for.

choices.text: Ask him what it is for

effects.log: 'Nothing,' he says. 'That is the beginning.' You spend a year learning what he meant and the sword gets quieter and faster.

choices.text: Pour his cup and say nothing

effects.log: He nods as if you had answered. Perhaps you had.

events.text: A night when the moon is full and the blade is in your hand without your having drawn it. You see the gap in every stance in the yard, including your own, including the moon's.

effects.log: The Sword Dao. From now on no feint fools your eyes and no tell is hidden from you. The murim has a name for people like you and it is not a kind one, only a true one.

choices.text: Sheathe the blade and go to bed

effects.log: You sleep very well. The understanding stays, gentler, and you are never again in a hurry with a sword.

events.text: You step off a roof without thinking and land without sound, and only when a child applauds do you realise you did not use the method. You simply went where the wind would have gone.

choices.text: Follow the wind for a season

effects.log: You walk where the wind walks: ridges, river mouths, the gaps between crowds. By winter you are somewhere else before anyone sees you leave.
The method is safe and good. The wind waits.

events.text: A storm on the mountain, and you walk into it because something in you wants to see whether the wind will carry a person who has stopped weighing anything.

ok.log: It does. The Dao of the Wind: a blow that would have landed finds nothing where you were. The murim calls you a ghost for the rest of your life.

fail.deathCause: a storm you walked into on purpose
fail.log: The wind has opinions about you. It throws you against the rock, and you come down soaked and bruised and a little wiser.

effects.log: The storm passes. You are very fast and very light and quite alive.

events.text: A poem comes to you entire while you watch a rival draw his blade, and you understand his whole life from the way he holds it: the father, the debt, the fear. You could write it down or cut it.

choices.text: Write it down and give it to him

effects.log: He reads it, and sheathes the blade, and weeps, and is your friend for decades.
You win the bout in one exchange because you knew where his fear would put his feet. The poem stays in your sleeve.

events.text: You have read a thousand people the way you read that one. On a quiet night it turns around: you read yourself, all of it, and do not look away.

effects.log: The Heart Dao. Nobody's rhythm breaks yours again, in a fight or out of one. People say talking to you is like being seen for the first time.
Some rooms stay closed. You are the finest reader of people in the murim, and nobody has read you.

events.text: A cart runs over your foot in the market and you notice because of the shouting. Your body has stopped reporting small things. The old body-tempering masters call this the first silence.

ok.log: Three months under a waterfall in winter. The body stops reporting large things too, and starts simply handling them.

fail.log: The waterfall wins. You come out shaking, and the second silence stays a rumour.

effects.log: A practical answer. Your body goes on being quietly extraordinary and you go on noticing the shouting.

events.text: A master of the Vajra Body offers to hit you as hard as he can, once, as a test or a lesson. He has killed two students this way. He is quite honest about it.

ok.log: You are moved back one step. He bows to the ground. The Iron Dao: blows that land on you land on something that does not care.

fail.deathCause: a single blow from a Vajra master
fail.log: He hits you, and the world goes. You wake days later to find him sitting by your bed, remarkably quiet.

effects.log: He respects that too. You remain very hard to hurt and very easy to live with.

events.text: You can taste a poison before it reaches your tongue now, and name it. A Tang elder, hearing this, sends you a cup. You name all seven.

ok.log: Nothing. Your body has made peace with poison the way a river makes peace with rain. The elder is delighted and a little afraid.

fail.log: The cup is stronger than your boast. You spend three days learning the names of poisons from the inside.

effects.log: The roses die. The elder laughs for a long time and sends a second cup, of tea.

events.text: The valley where every plant kills. The Ten Thousand Poison Valley's founders walked through it once, barefoot, and came out as something else. The path is still there.

ok.log: You come out of the valley on the fourth day. Nothing that grows can hurt you, and everything you touch in a fight carries a little of the valley with it.

fail.deathCause: the valley where every plant kills
fail.log: The valley takes its toll on the fourth day, and you crawl out on your hands, poisoned in places you never knew could be.

effects.log: You know every poison there is and none of them know you. That is enough mastery for one life.

events.text: You set a farmer's broken arm and feel, for a moment, the bone wanting to knit, as if you could simply ask it to. You ask. It does, a month early.

choices.text: Ask again, with the next patient

effects.log: It works often enough that the medicine hall starts calling you something you ask them not to.

choices.text: Call it luck and use splints

effects.log: A good physician with a very good luck. The asking waits.

events.text: A patient the texts say is dead: no pulse, no breath, warm. You can feel the thread of life in her, thin as a hair, and you can feel where it wants to go.

ok.log: She breathes on the third hour. The Dao of Living Things: your own wounds close faster than they should, and the dying come to your door from three provinces.

fail.deathCause: holding another's life thread too long
fail.log: The thread slips. You hold on a breath too long, and the cost comes out of you instead.

effects.log: You close her eyes. You are the best physician alive, and you know where the line is, and you keep it.

events.text: Over a game of go with a stranger, you see the whole of the next forty moves and, for a moment, the whole of the stranger's next forty years. He loses the game. You lose your appetite.

choices.text: Play on, and tell him what you saw

effects.log: He changes two of the forty years because of what you told him, and writes to you when the rest come true.
Some things are better not seen. You do not play go for a year, and see them anyway.

events.text: A war is coming to the province and both sides send for you. From a hilltop you can see how it ends, and how it could end instead, and that the second needs one person to be in the wrong place at the right time.

ok.log: The war ends a year early and a thousand people fewer die. Nobody knows why except you. The Dao of the Board: you see three moves ahead of anyone, in a fight or a court.

fail.deathCause: standing in the right place in a war
fail.log: The right place turns out to be the wrong one. You come out of the war with a scar and the wrong side's thanks.

choices.text: Advise one side and go home

effects.log: They win. The war takes the year it was always going to take. You are the most sought-after strategist in the murim.

events.text: You hum while sharpening a blade and the blade sings back, and a crack you did not know was in it opens along the note. A blind musician in the market hears it and finds you by the sound.

effects.log: One note, held correctly, finds the crack in anything: a blade, a wall, a liar's story.

choices.text: Buy him a meal and keep your blade

effects.log: He eats and plays and tells you the note will find you when it is ready.

events.text: The great bell of the mountain temple has not rung since the war. The monks say it is cracked. You can hear that it is not: it is waiting for a note.

ok.log: The bell answers across three valleys. The Dao of One Note: your voice carries into the fight and takes the rhythm out of anyone who hears it.

fail.log: The bell does not answer. Your voice cracks on the third breath, and the monks politely study their sandals.

effects.log: The monks thank you for not trying. You go on knowing the note and using it only for blades and liars.
